name: @lasercode/desktop
description: Electron shell: main process, tray, notifications, keychain, updater. Spawns the host from a bundled stock Node placed outside asar (M5-T2). Must not import Pi.

scripts.clean: rm -rf dist *.tsbuildinfo out build/icon.png build/icons build/linux/generated
scripts.prepack:app: pnpm run build && pnpm run icons && pnpm run linux:assets && node scripts/fetch-node.mjs --current

//optionalDependencies: @napi-rs/keyring resolves its native binding with a bare `require()` of a
per-platform sibling package, declared as an optionalDependency of the
keyring package itself. electron-builder builds the packaged node_modules
tree by walking *manifests*, and under pnpm's isolated store it does not
follow that hop: the packaged app got `@napi-rs/keyring` and no binding,
and died at startup with `Cannot find native binding` — after a twenty
minute build, on a machine that developed and tested perfectly.
Declaring the bindings here makes them the desktop package's own direct
dependencies, so the walker sees them, they carry exact pins like
everything else laser ships, and `build/before-pack.cjs` can check them.
They are optional and carry `os`/`cpu` fields, so each build machine
installs only its own — which is why a release builds each architecture on
a runner of that architecture rather than cross-compiling.
